correctness.rationale: Every acyclic orientation of each labeled complete multipartite graph of order at most 7 appears as an orientation of a total topological order; every one-edge flip giving another DAG corresponds to a one-skeleton edge. A dimension n-1 vertex is simple exactly when its reversal degree is n-1. The included exact standalone finite checker generates all 25 relevant unordered part-size partitions, tests all neighbor flips and runs exhaustive BFS of the induced simple states. Both exception masks are rederived by a second full edge-mask enumeration with Kahn DAG detection, and an isolated witness is explicitly checked. An independent nonnegative block-degree identity supplies a structural cross-check. This is a finite exhaustive proof only, with no unverified n>=8 assertion.

value.rationale: The induced connectedness of simple zonotope vertices is a natural singularity/face-incidence invariant, already known to behave differently for complete-split versus complete-bipartite graphs. The finite theorem determines the sharp first failure among all multipartite graphs with at least three parts and gives two structurally different minimal counterexamples: a 430+430 split and 1192+48 frozen components. The result is a motivated complete natural cutoff, not an arbitrary isolated numerical slice or re-tabulation of orientation counts; it makes no unsupported claims for larger graphs.
